issues.detail: Both claims cite simulation_parameters, whose statement imports the Table-I default T=1. Ei_scaling_T_low simultaneously cites temperature_T_low with T=10^-6, so the historical branch has mutually inconsistent fixed conditions. Revise the card by removing temperature from the common condition (and preferably omitting global settings not needed to interpret this response), while retaining T=10^-6 and T=1 only as disjoint branch-specific conditions.

The selected readout is E_i evaluated at t_eq, but the card only names equilibration time and does not preserve how it is determined. Add a common fixed condition linked by both claims: t_eq is t2 after the global maximum of the second derivative of N_C/L^2, with the subsequent interval defined by d^2(N_C/L^2)/dt^2 <= -Delta and Delta equal to 10% of that maximum. This source-defined rule is necessary to make the readout condition objective; do not substitute the separate fitted scaling law for t_eq.

The tau_Q control definition says that chemical potential is linearly ramped from mu_i to mu_f, but its selected anchors only support the fitted response/domain. Add lines 156-157 (or an equivalent exact locator) to anchor the control definition and retain the quench protocol as a common condition if it is used downstream.

The mechanism statement attributes the exponent to the quench-time scaling of vortex number and background density, but its anchors omit the main-text passage that states rho proportional to tau_Q^{-1/(1+z nu)}, n_v proportional to tau_Q^{-2 nu/(1+z nu)}, and combines them. Add lines 289-329 so the stated derivation, rather than only its final equation and end-matter recap, is directly supported.
